items.title: Michael Abene interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 11, 2003
items.q: And I wrote with Gary when he used to have a company called Sky Records years ago.

ctx.x: Yeah, it’s all the same to me at one point. The funniest thing is when I’m writing for strings for some reason the hardest instrument is the viola sometimes. And I’m thinking wait, now I can transpose like any instrument but why do I always sometimes have trouble with the viola? Years ago, one of the unsung heroes of jazz composing for me was Gary McFarland. And I wrote with Gary when he used to have a company called Sky Records years ago. So I would write with Gary, if I was hung up with something he
would conduct my session. But he wrote concert scores and it would drive me nuts when I had to answer a question, I’d look at the note I’d say wait — I’m hearing it in another key.
